title: SpaceX IPO Expands to $85.7 Billion After Underwriters Exercise Greenshoe Option

author.name: Alex Thorne
author.bio: Alex covers Wall Street, corporate finance, and emerging market trends.

excerpt: SpaceX’s record-breaking IPO grew to $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised the greenshoe option, highlighting extraordinary investor demand for Elon Musk’s aerospace company.

content.text: SpaceX’s record-breaking initial public offering grew even larger after underwriters exercised the greenshoe option, pushing the total value of the deal to about $85.7 billion. This came just days after the aerospace company completed what was already the largest IPO in U.S. history.

Strong demand from both institutional and retail investors allowed banks managing the transaction to sell additional shares beyond the original allocation. Analysts said the overallotment reflected continuing confidence in SpaceX’s long-term growth and reinforced the company’s reputation as a leader in the global space industry.

Market observers described the expansion as a signal that demand still far exceeded the number of shares available. Even after shattering previous fundraising records, investors remained eager to buy in. The enlarged IPO strengthened SpaceX’s position as one of the most valuable publicly traded companies in both technology and aerospace.

The greenshoe option (or overallotment option) is a clause contained in the underwriting agreement of an IPO that allows the underwriters to sell more shares than originally planned, if demand is higher than expected. In SpaceX’s case, banks exercised this option after receiving a huge number of orders from investors seeking to get into the company.

This is a common mechanism in large public offerings. It is used to help stabilize trading and also gives the banks some flexibility if there is more demand from investors than there is supply. By using the option, the underwriters were able to meet demand without unduly disrupting the market.
The move highlighted the high level of investor interest in SpaceX and the aggressive buying of shares after the company’s market debut.

The appeal is driven largely by the company’s leadership position in commercial space launches and the rapid growth of its Starlink satellite internet business. SpaceX has established a dominant position with reusable rocket technology, government contracts and an expanding portfolio of commercial launches.

The company’s global customer base is growing, offering strong long-term revenue opportunities, and investors also highlight SpaceX’s big future plans including next-generation spacecraft and more space exploration. Starlink is viewed as a major growth driver.
These prospects have made SpaceX one of the most closely watched companies in global markets. Demand for its shares reflects both its technological advantage and potential for continued growth.
Historic IPO Signifies Faith in Public Markets

The IPO is viewed as a landmark event for capital markets after years of uneven activity. Analysts say SpaceX’s strong debut could encourage other large private companies to consider public listings if market conditions remain favorable.

The offering showed that investors are still willing to commit substantial capital to companies they see as leaders in advanced technology and transformative industries. Market observers said the scale of the IPO, combined with the exercise of the greenshoe, signals confidence in both SpaceX and the broader outlook for growth-focused investments.

The IPO is already one of the market's headline events of 2026 and investors will be watching SpaceX's financials. The surge to $85.7 billion shows the huge demand for SpaceX shares and the company’s growing presence in aerospace, communications and technology.
